title: Encapsulate Record

solutions.title: A class with three getters, not a public interface
solutions.tradeoff: Four fields still have no public getter because no caller reads them yet - the class is smaller than the record it replaced, and the next caller that needs one has to add it, not assume it is already there.

reviewFocus: Can any file outside loan.ts still write `dueOn`, `returnedOn`, or `renewalCount` directly - by import, not by convention? A private field TypeScript refuses to compile against is the only version of this that counts.
Does every public getter answer a question an existing caller in this exercise actually asks, or did one get added speculatively for a future caller that does not exist yet?

`renew` reads `returnedOn` and `renewalCount` and then, on the same call, writes `dueOn` and `renewalCount`. Encapsulating the record did not remove that internal coupling - it only gave the whole sequence one name. Is that in scope here, or is it the next refactoring?
Is `id` still derived the same way in both the challenge and the solution? A refactor that quietly changes what makes a loan's identity is a behaviour change wearing a structural one.

Compare this solution's getter set to drill-06-06's: that drill rejected a getter for the whole settings record. Does this solution's `Loan` avoid the same trap, or does something read all three private fields through one call?
